'''Killian Hayes''' (born 27 July 2001) is a French-American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[ratiopharm Ulm]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL). Standing {{height|m=1.96}}, he mainly plays the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] position.

The son of an American basketball player, Hayes was born in [[Lakeland, Florida]] but grew up in France due to his father's professional career. From a young age, Hayes played with French club [[Cholet Basket|Cholet]] and excelled at the junior level. He debuted for Cholet's senior team at age 16 before receiving regular playing time in the following season. In 2019–20, he moved to Germany to play for Ulm.

Hayes won the gold medal and earned [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors with [[France national under-17 basketball team|France]] at the [[2017 FIBA U16 European Championship]]. He led his team to a silver medal at the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|2018 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]].

== Early life and career ==
Hayes was born in [[Lakeland, Florida]] in the United States, in the same hospital as his father, DeRon Hayes, who was playing basketball in the [[American Basketball Association (2000–present)|American Basketball Association]] (ABA) at the time.<ref name="proux">{{cite web |last1=Proux |first1=Jérémy |title=Avec le fils, les Hayes font la paire |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/pays-de-la-loire/maine-et-loire/avec-le-fils-les-hayes-font-la-paire-4805139 |website=[[Ouest-France]] |accessdate=14 January 2020 |language=French |date=14 February 2017}}</ref> One year later, Hayes began living in [[Cholet]], France after his father continued his career in the [[LNB Pro A]], the country's top league. He played basketball from an early age, facing older opponents and often playing [[pick-up game]]s in Lakeland and [[Orlando, Florida]]. Hayes watched highlights of basketball games on [[YouTube]], drawing inspiration from basketball player [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[AND1 Live Tour|AND1 mixtapes]], to learn new [[basketball moves|moves]]. He grew up playing for [[Cholet Basket]], his father's former club, at the youth level. Although he wanted to play high school and [[college basketball]] in the United States, he remained in France upon the advice of his father, who had come from the American basketball system.<ref name=gardner/>

In 2016, Hayes turned down an opportunity to join [[INSEP]], a prestigious sports institute in [[Paris]], upon his parents' guidance. He began playing for Espoirs Cholet in LNB Espoirs, the French under-21 league, in the 2016–17 season and was five to seven years younger than many of his opponents.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |last2=Schmitz |first2=Mike |title=Jordan Brand Classic Global Showcase Scouting Reports 2020 |language=French |date=16 February 2017}}</ref> In seven Espoirs games, Hayes averaged 4.7 [[Point (basketball)|points]] and 2.3 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] in 15.4 minutes per game.<ref seven assists and five [[Steal (basketball)|steals]], sharing [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors with Addison Patterson, at the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International Game.<ref>{{Cite |language=French |access-date=27 January 2018}}</ref> In the 2017–18 season, Hayes averaged 16.6 points, 3.9 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 7.2 assists per game for Espoirs Cholet.<ref == Professional career ==
===Cholet (2017–2019)===
[[File:Killian Hayes.jpg|thumb|left|Hayes with [[Cholet Basket|Cholet]] in 2018]]
Hayes made his debut with the [[Cholet Basket|Cholet]] senior team on 21 October 2017 at 16 years, two months and 24 days of age, playing two minutes in a loss to [[Nanterre 92]] in the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1= Rutard |first1= Sacha |url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/411774/killian-hayes-cholet-16-ans-est-entre-en-jeu-en-pro-a/|title=Killian Hayes (Cholet), 16 ans, est entré en jeu en Pro A|work=Basket Europe|access-date=2018-01-27|language=fr-FR}}</ref> In February 2018, he played in the [[Basketball Without Borders]] camp during [[2018 NBA All-Star Game#All-Star Weekend|NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[Los Angeles]], where he was the second-youngest participant.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Basketball Without Borders: Camp preview and full roster reveal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22360171/2018-basketball-borders-preview-full-rosters-nba-draft |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=26 March 2020 |date=8 February 2018}}</ref> In his Pro A season finale on 15 May 2018, Hayes recorded 12 points and six assists in a win over [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket|Le Mans]] for his best performance of the season.<ref name="guern">{{cite web |last1=Guern |first1=Thomas |title=Killian Hayes, le prodige de Cholet, "réfléchit à toutes les options" |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/basket/basket-killian-hayes-le-prodige-de-cholet-reflechit-toutes-les-options-5760594 |website=[[Ouest-France]] |accessdate=2 January 2020 |language=French |date=15 May 2018}}</ref> He finished the season averaging 2.2 points and 1.2 assists in 9.1 minutes per game, through nine appearances.<ref name="realgm">{{cite web |title=Killian Hayes Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Killian-Hayes/Summary/108654 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=July 26, 2018}}</ref>

Before the [[2018–19 Pro A season|2018–19 season]], he signed a three-year professional contract with Cholet after considering various other European clubs.<ref name="proux2">{{cite web |last1=Proux |first1=Jérémy |title=Killian Hayes, les coulisses d'une "négo" |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/pays-de-la-loire/cholet-49300/killian-hayes-les-coulisses-d-une-nego-5852074 |website=[[Ouest-France]] |accessdate=2 January 2019 |language=French |date=28 June 2018}}</ref> On 22 September 2018, after missing three weeks with back and toe injuries, Hayes scored 12 points in a loss to [[SIG Basket|Strasbourg]] in his first appearance of the season.<ref name="rutard">{{cite web |last1=Rutard |first1=Sacha |title=Cholet: Après trois semaines d’absence, Killian Hayes revient ce soir contre Strasbourg |url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/440824/cholet-apres-trois-semaines-dabsence-killian-hayes-revient-ce-soir-contre-strasbourg/ |website=Basket Europe |accessdate=2 January 2020 |language=French |date=22 September 2018}}</ref> After his team was last place in its league early in the season, it parted ways with head coach Régis Boissié, who was replaced by [[Erman Kunter]]. Due to Cholet's struggles, Hayes initially believed he had "made a huge mistake by staying in Europe."<ref name=gardner/> At [[2019 NBA All-Star Game#All-Star Weekend|2019 NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]] in February, he competed at the Basketball Without Borders camp for the second time.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Woo |first1=Jeremy |title=The Best NBA Draft Prospects at 2019 Basketball Without Borders |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2019/02/18/basketball-without-borders-nba-draft-prospects-deni-avdija-khalifa-diop-all-star-weekend |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=26 March 2020 |date=18 February 2019}}</ref> On 30 May 2019, Hayes tallied a season-high 17 points, five rebounds and five steals in a loss to [[Élan Chalon]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mar 30, 2019 - Cholet 84 at Chalon-Sur-Saone 89 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2019-03-30/Cholet-Basket-at-Chalon-Sur-Saone/331635 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=2 January 2020 |date=30 March 2019}}</ref> In 34 games, Hayes averaged 7.1 points and 3.1 assists per game.<ref name="gardner">{{cite web |last1=Gardner |first1=David |title=Killian Hayes Is Coming to Claim His Basketball Birthright |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2847971-killian-hayes-is-coming-to-claim-his-basketball-birthright |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=3 January 2019 |date=2 August 2019}}</ref>

===Ulm (2019–2020)===
On 2 August 2019, Hayes signed a three-year contract with [[ratiopharm Ulm]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL), the top league in Germany, and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ulm gives the ball to teen guard Hayes |url=https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/9ud9sh38hc9uwe9j/ulm-gives-the-ball-to-teen-guard-hayes |publisher=[[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] |accessdate=2 August 2019 |date=2 August 2019}}</ref> He debuted on 24 September, posting 15 points, six rebounds and six assists in a win over [[SC Rasta Vechta|Rasta Vechta]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Neuzugang Killian Hayes führt Ulm zum Sieg gegen Vechta |url=https://www.swr.de/sport/mehr-sport/basketball/ratiopharm-ulm/Basketball-Neuzugang-Killian-Hayes-fuehrt-Ulm-zum-Sieg-gegen-Vechta,ratiopharm-ulm-gegen-rasta-vechta-100.html |website=[[Südwestrundfunk]] |accessdate=20 December 2019 |language=German |date=24 September 2019}}</ref> Hayes played his first EuroCup game on 2 October, finishing with eight points, nine assists and three steals in a loss to [[Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna|Virtus Bologna]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Virtus makes EuroCup return with win at Ulm |url=https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/games/results/showgame?gamecode=3&seasoncode=U2019#!report |publisher=[[EuroCup Basketball]] |accessdate=20 December 2019 |date=2 October 2019}}</ref> On 3 November, he recorded his first career [[double (basketball)|double-double]], with 11 points and 11 assists in a loss to [[Alba Berlin]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nov 3, 2019 - Ratiopharm Ulm 89, ALBA Berlin 109 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2019-11-03/Ratiopharm-Ulm-at-ALBA-Berlin/339252 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=20 December 2019 |date=3 November 2019}}</ref> Two weeks later, Hayes scored a then career-high 24 points, along with five assists and three steals, in an 81–78 victory over [[Brose Bamberg]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola |title=Show di Killian Hayes contro il Bamberg: career-high da 24 punti |url=https://sportando.basketball/show-di-killian-hayes-contro-il-bamberg-career-high-da-24-punti/ |publisher=Sportando |accessdate=15 February 2020 |language=Italian |date=17 November 2019}}</ref> On 20 November, he tallied 12 points and 11 assists in a loss to [[Promitheas Patras B.C.|Promitheas Patras]], becoming the second-youngest player to ever register a double-double in the EuroCup, the youngest being [[Ricky Rubio]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Promitheas wins, eliminates Ulm |url=https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/games/results/showgame?gamecode=86&seasoncode=U2019#!report |publisher=[[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] |accessdate=20 December 2019 |date=20 November 2019}}</ref> Hayes established a new career-high in scoring on 18 December with 25 points, five three-pointers and five assists in a 96–92 defeat to [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]].<ref name="brouet">{{cite web |last1=Brouet |first1=Christophe |title=Killian Hayes marque les esprits en vue de la draft avec une grosse performance en EuroCup |url=https://basket-infos.com/2019/12/19/killian-hayes-marque-les-esprits-en-vue-de-la-draft-avec-une-grosse-performance-en-eurocup/ |publisher=Basket-Infos |accessdate=15 February 2020 |language=French |date=19 December 2019}}</ref> He recorded 20 points and 10 assists in a 112–106 [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] loss to Alba Berlin on 11 February.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alba wins shootout, Gottingen triumphs over Bayern |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/bbl/1021240/alba-wins-shootout-gottingen-triumphs-over-bayern/ |publisher=EuroHoops |accessdate=15 February 2020 |date=11 February 2020}}</ref> When the BBL was suspended on March 8 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic|coronavirus pandemic]], Hayes returned to his family in Lakeland. On March 27, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref name="draft">{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=PG Killian Hayes entering NBA draft, 'excited' |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28962394/pg-killian-hayes-entering-nba-draft-excited |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=March 27, 2020 |date=March 27, 2020}}</ref> Hayes did not play in the [[2019–20 Basketball Bundesliga#End of season tournament|BBL Final Tournament]] held that June.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Top NBA prospect Killian Hayes won't play in German league finale |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29151126/top-nba-prospect-killian-hayes-play-german-league-finale |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=August 8, 2020 |date=May 8, 2020}}</ref> He finished the season averaging 11.6 points, 5.4 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game through 33 combined games in the EuroCup, BBL and [[BBL-Pokal]].<ref name=realgm/>

== National team career ==
Representing [[France national under-17 basketball team|France]], Hayes was named MVP of the [[2017 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Podgorica]], Montenegro.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/news/frances-hayes-named-mvp-headlines-all-star-five1|title=France's Hayes named MVP, headlines All-Star Five|website=FIBA.basketball|language=en|access-date=2018-01-27}}</ref> He averaged 16.6 points, seven rebounds and 5.1 assists per game and led his team to a gold medal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/Killian-Hayes|title=Killian HAYES at the FIBA U16 European Championship Division A 2017 - FIBA.basketball|website=FIBA.basketball|language=en|access-date=2018-01-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/news/-crowned-u16-european-champions|title=France crowned U16 European champions|website=FIBA.basketball|language=en|access-date=2018-01-27}}</ref> At the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]] in Argentina, Hayes won a silver medal and was named to the All-Star Five after averaging 16.1 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 2.7 steals per game.<ref name=realgm/> In July 2019, the [[French Federation of Basketball]] imposed a six-game suspension on Hayes for not playing in the [[2019 FIBA U20 European Championship]] in [[Tel Aviv]], Israel.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ratiopharm Ulm signs possible lottery pick Killian Hayes |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/914772/ratiopharm-ulm-signs-possible-lottery-pick-killian-hayes/ |website=EuroHoops |accessdate=30 January 2020 |date=2 August 2019}}</ref>

== Player profile ==
[[File:Killian Hayes Brandyn Curry (cropped).jpg|thumb|Hayes (left), with Cholet, defends [[ESSM Le Portel|Le Portel]]'s [[Brandyn Curry]] in November 2018.]]
Hayes primarily functions as a [[point guard]].<ref name="magnotti">{{cite web |last1=Magnotti |first1=Trevor |title=Is Killian Hayes an NBA point guard? |url=https://fansided.com/2019/12/02/killian-hayes-nba-draft-2020-lead-ball-handler/ |publisher=FanSided |accessdate=25 March 2020 |date=2 December 2019}}</ref> Listed at a height of {{height|m=1.96}}, he possesses exceptional size for his position, although he is not regarded by analysts as an extraordinary athlete.<ref name="tjarks">{{cite web |last1=Tjarks |first1=Jonathan |title=Will NBA Teams Lean Overseas in the 2020 NBA Draft? |url=https://www.theringer.com/nba/2020/3/5/21166020/nba-draft-2020-european-prospects |website=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]] |accessdate=25 March 2020 |date=5 March 2020}}</ref><ref name="berman">{{cite web |last1=Berman |first1=Marc |title=Hidden point-guard gem Killian Hayes may be answer for Knicks |url=https://nypost.com/2020/03/22/hidden-point-guard-gem-killian-hayes-may-be-answer-for-knicks/ |website=[[New York Post]] |accessdate=March 25, 2020 |date=March 22, 2020}}</ref><ref name="ulm">{{cite web |title=Killian Hayes |url=https://ratiopharmulm.com/team/spieler/killian-hayes-45731/ |publisher=[[ratiopharm Ulm]] |accessdate=25 March 2020 |language=German}}</ref> Hayes is [[handedness|left-handed]] and rarely handles the ball with his right hand, which sometimes limits him. He models his offensive game after that of [[James Harden]], another left-handed guard.<ref name="strauss">{{cite web |last1=Strauss |first1=Ethan |title=French prospect Killian Hayes could be special and is a Warriors name to watch in the 2020 draft |url=https://theathletic.com/1604862/2020/02/13/french-prospect-killian-hayes-could-be-special-and-is-a-warriors-name-to-watch-in-the-2020-draft/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |accessdate=25 March 2020 |date=13 February 2020}}</ref> Hayes has drawn the most praise for his playmaking repertoire. In February 2020, ''[[The Athletic]]'' writer Sam Vecenie said that "his vision is absolutely off the charts, and his ability to complete passes off of a live dribble with his left hand is unbelievable out of ball screens."<ref name="vecenie">{{cite web |last1=Vecenie |first1=Sam |title=Vecenie’s 2020 NBA Draft Big Board, 3.0: The internationals make their move |url=https://theathletic.com/1635879/2020/02/28/vecenies-2020-nba-draft-big-board-3-0-the-internationals-make-their-move/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |accessdate=25 March 2020 |date=28 February 2020}}</ref> Hayes thrives as a [[pick and roll]] ball-handler and is comfortable operating in a half-court offense.<ref name=tjarks/> At the same time, he can be prone to [[Turnover (basketball)|turning the ball over]].<ref name=strauss/> Hayes displays good shooting form and often attempts [[basketball moves#Step-back jump shot|step-back jump shots]], but his [[Three-point field goal|three-point]] shooting is considered a work in progress.<ref name="cohen">{{cite web |last1=Cohen |first1=Zachary |title=Taking A Look At The 2020 NBA Draft’s Five Best International Prospects |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/zacharycohen/2020/02/24/taking-a-look-at-the-2020-nba-drafts-five-best-international-prospects/#2786129b39bb |website=[[Forbes]] |accessdate=25 March 2020 |date=24 February 2020}}</ref> He excels in shooting off the dribble as opposed to in catch-and-shoot situations.<ref name=tjarks/> Hayes is an accurate [[free throw]] shooter and has good touch around the basket, with an advanced [[Basketball moves#Tear drop|floater]].<ref name=magnotti/><ref name=cohen/> He can guard [[shooting guard]]s and smaller-sized [[small forward]]s. While his lack of lateral quickness prevents him from being a great perimeter defender, he is more effective as an off-ball and pick and roll defender.<ref name="milner">{{cite web |last1=Milner |first1=Zach |last2=Pearlman |first2=Spencer |title=Killian Hayes Scouting Report (Collaboration) |url=https://www.thestepien.com/2020/02/14/killian-hayes-scouting-report-collaboration/ |publisher=The Stepien |accessdate=15 February 2020 |date=14 February 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Hayes has an American father, DeRon Hayes, who played [[college basketball]] as a [[forward (basketball)|forward]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State Nittany Lions]] in the early 1990s and left as one of the program's most prolific scorers.<ref name=gardner/><ref>{{cite web |title=Postgame Notes: Penn State 63, Minnesota 58 |url=https://gopsusports.com/news/2015/1/28/Postgame_Notes_Penn_State_63_Minnesota_58.aspx |publisher=Penn State University Athletics |accessdate=25 March 2020 |date=28 January 2015}}</ref> DeRon played professionally in France, Portugal, Sweden, Ukraine and Russia.<ref name=sang/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/pays-de-la-loire/mayenne/killian-hayes-nba-et-jo-2024-dans-le-viseur-5211735|title=Killian Hayes, NBA et JO 2024 dans le viseur|work=[[Ouest-France]]|access-date=2018-01-27|language=fr-FR}}</ref> He spent much of the prime years of his career with French clubs Cholet and [[SLUC Nancy Basket|SLUC Nancy]].<ref>{{cite web |title=DeRon Hayes : retour attendu, pas encore payant |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/pays-de-la-loire/deron-hayes-retour-attendu-pas-encore-payant-1749458 |website=[[Ouest-France]] |accessdate=26 March 2020 |language=French |date=26 November 2013}}</ref> Hayes' mother, Sandrine (née Demiannay), is a native of [[Cholet]], France and is a former basketball player as well.<ref name="cholet">{{cite web |title=Killian Hayes |url=https://www.cholet-basket.com/personne/killian-hayes |publisher=[[Cholet Basket]] |accessdate=26 March 2020 |language=French}}</ref> His parents met because his mother was the sister of the girlfriend of his father's teammate.<ref name=gardner/>
